beta.def: a number showing how much a share price moves compared with the market
beta.ex: Shares with a high beta usually rise and fall more sharply than the market.

summit.def: an official meeting between leaders of governments or organisations
summit.ex: The trade summit brought together ministers from twelve countries.

repay.def: to pay back money that you have borrowed
repay.ex: The company plans to repay the loan within five years.

outsider.def: a person who is not part of a particular group, organisation or company
outsider.ex: The board appointed an outsider as chief executive to bring in fresh ideas.

offshore.ex: Many manufacturers have moved production to offshore factories to cut costs.
offshore.def: located or registered in another country, often to pay less tax

lag.def: a period of delay between one event and another
lag.ex: There is often a time lag between placing an order and receiving the goods.

headline.def: the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters
headline.ex: The merger made the headlines in every business newspaper.

macroeconomic.ex: The central bank publishes macroeconomic forecasts every quarter.
macroeconomic.def: relating to the economy as a whole

contingency.def: an event that might happen in the future and that you need to plan for
contingency.ex: We have set aside extra funds for any contingency during the project.

median.def: the middle value in a set of numbers arranged in order
median.ex: The median salary in the department rose by four percent last year.

receiver.def: a person or organisation that receives something; also part of a telephone
receiver.ex: Please check that the receiver's address is correct before you send the parcel.

abolish.def: to officially end a law, system or practice
abolish.ex: The government voted to abolish the tax on small businesses.

lure.ex: The retailer used heavy discounts to lure shoppers away from its competitors.

spy.def: to watch someone or something secretly in order to get information
spy.ex: The company was accused of spying on its competitors' research.

liquidate.def: to close a business and sell everything it owns in order to pay its debts
liquidate.ex: The firm was forced to liquidate after it lost its biggest client.

exclusion.def: the act of not allowing someone or something to take part or be included
exclusion.ex: The policy contains several exclusions, so read the contract carefully.

dot.def: a small round mark or spot
dot.ex: Our company website address is lexkite dot com, written without any spaces.

hub.def: the central or most important part of an area, system or activity
hub.ex: Singapore is a major shipping and financial hub in Asia.

echo.def: a repeated sound; also an opinion that repeats an earlier one
echo.ex: Her report echoes the concerns that staff raised at last month's meeting.

petty.ex: Please keep receipts for any petty cash you spend on office supplies.

notable.def: important or interesting enough to deserve attention
notable.ex: The most notable change this year was the move to online ordering.

originate.def: to begin or be created in a particular place or way
originate.ex: The idea for the product originated in a staff suggestion box.

predictor.ex: Customer satisfaction is a strong predictor of future sales.
predictor.def: something that helps to show what will happen

peg.def: a fixed level at which the value of a currency or price is kept
peg.ex: The country kept its currency peg to the US dollar for many years.

woe.ex: Rising fuel costs have added to the airline's financial woes.

commentator.def: a person who gives opinions about events on television, radio or in newspapers
commentator.ex: Several business commentators predicted that interest rates would rise.

salvage.ex: The new manager managed to salvage the deal at the last minute.
salvage.def: the act of saving something from damage or loss

doom.def: a terrible future situation that you cannot avoid
doom.ex: Despite the talk of doom, sales actually rose in the final quarter.

smuggle.ex: Customs officers check containers to stop people smuggling goods into the country.
smuggle.def: to take goods into or out of a country illegally

cheaply.ex: The new machines allow us to produce spare parts more cheaply.

pit.def: a large hole in the ground, for example where minerals are dug out
pit.ex: The construction team dug a deep pit for the building's foundations.

annum.def: year (used in the phrase per annum, meaning 'each year')
annum.ex: The position offers a salary of 45,000 dollars per annum.

mar.def: to spoil something or make it less good
mar.ex: The product launch was marred by technical problems.

reportedly.def: according to what people say or what is reported
reportedly.ex: The company is reportedly planning to open three new stores.

maneuver.def: a clever or careful action done to gain an advantage
maneuver.ex: The merger was a smart maneuver to enter the Asian market.

credential.def: a qualification, achievement or document that shows you are suitable for something
credential.ex: All applicants must send copies of their professional credentials.

peacekeeping.ex: The organisation funds peacekeeping and humanitarian projects around the world.
peacekeeping.def: the work of keeping peace between groups or countries that have been in conflict

decimal.def: a number expressed using a decimal point, such as 0.5 or 2.75
decimal.ex: Please round all prices to two decimal places.

leverage.def: using borrowed money to increase possible profits; also power to influence
leverage.ex: The company used leverage to finance the takeover of its main competitor.

diversify.def: to develop a wider range of products, services or investments in order to reduce risk
diversify.ex: The firm decided to diversify into renewable energy.

thereafter.ex: The contract runs for one year and may be renewed annually thereafter.

triple.ex: Online sales have tripled since the company launched its app.
triple.def: three times as much or as many

bidder.ex: The building was sold to the highest bidder at the auction.
bidder.def: a person or company that offers money in an auction or for a contract

saver.ex: Higher interest rates are good news for savers.

flotation.ex: The company raised two million dollars through its stock market flotation.
flotation.def: the first sale of a company's shares on the stock market

affiliate.def: to officially connect a smaller company or organisation with a larger one
affiliate.ex: The clinic is affiliated with the city hospital.

capitalize.def: to use a situation to gain an advantage (capitalize on something)
capitalize.ex: The company capitalized on the growing demand for electric bikes.

blend.def: to mix two or more things together
blend.ex: The new tea blends green tea with dried fruit.

deprive.def: to take something important away from someone (deprive somebody of something)
deprive.ex: Long hours deprive staff of time with their families.

fret.def: to worry about something, especially when it is not necessary
fret.ex: There is no need to fret about the interview; you are well prepared.

intrigue.def: to make someone very interested or curious
intrigue.ex: The unusual design of the new product intrigued many potential investors.

launder.def: to hide the illegal origin of money by passing it through legal businesses
launder.ex: Criminals tried to launder money through the property market.

arbitrage.def: buying something in one market and selling it at a higher price in another
arbitrage.ex: Traders use arbitrage to profit from small price differences between markets.

convertible.def: able to be changed into another form, such as shares
convertible.ex: The bank issued convertible bonds that investors can later exchange for shares.

ambition.def: a strong wish to achieve success, power or a particular goal
ambition.ex: Her ambition is to run her own company.

trustee.def: a person or organisation that legally controls money or property for others
trustee.ex: The trustees decide how the charity's money is spent.

sack.def: a large bag made of strong material, used for storing and carrying goods
sack.ex: He was sacked for being late too often.

installment.def: one of a series of regular payments that together pay for something
installment.ex: You can pay for the laptop in twelve monthly installments.

queue.def: a line of people or vehicles waiting for something
queue.ex: There was a long queue at the bank.

commander.def: a person who is in charge of a group, especially in the armed forces
commander.ex: The ship's commander gave the order to leave the port.

liquidation.def: the process of closing a company and selling its assets to pay its debts
liquidation.ex: The construction company went into liquidation after losing its largest contract.

macroeconomics.def: the study of a whole economy, including total output, income, employment and prices
macroeconomics.ex: Macroeconomics studies issues such as inflation, unemployment and national growth.

sacrifice.def: the act of giving up something valuable in order to get something more important
sacrifice.ex: He made many sacrifices to build his business.

acre.def: a unit for measuring land, equal to about 4,047 square metres
acre.ex: The organic farm covers two hundred acres of land near the river.

shield.def: something that protects a person or thing from harm or danger
shield.ex: Good insurance acts as a shield that protects the company from large losses.

encyclopedia.def: a book or website with information on many subjects, usually arranged in alphabetical order
encyclopedia.ex: The online encyclopedia is updated every day by thousands of volunteer editors.

contemplate.def: to think carefully about something, especially a possible future action
contemplate.ex: The company is contemplating a move to Singapore.

prospectus.def: a document describing a company or course to people who may invest or join
prospectus.ex: The university sends a prospectus to every applicant.

tort.def: a wrong act, other than breaking a contract, for which a person can be sued
tort.ex: Negligence is the most common type of tort.

succession.def: the process of one person taking over a role after another
succession.ex: The company has a clear plan for succession when the current director retires.

cotton.def: a soft white natural fibre from a plant, used to make cloth
cotton.ex: The factory produces cotton shirts for several well-known clothing brands.

helicopter.def: an aircraft with turning blades on top that can fly straight up
helicopter.ex: The energy company uses a helicopter to inspect its power lines every year.

conspiracy.def: a secret plan by a group of people to do something illegal or harmful
conspiracy.ex: The novel is about a conspiracy inside a large company.

census.def: an official count of a country's population
census.ex: The national census takes place every ten years.

disposition.def: a person's natural character; also the way something is arranged or sold
disposition.ex: The new receptionist has a calm and friendly disposition.
disposition.vi: tính khí; cách sắp xếp, xử lý (tài sản)

sensitivity.def: the ability to notice and react to small changes, or to understand other people's feelings

maturity.ex: The government bond reaches maturity in ten years, when investors are repaid in full.
maturity.def: the date when an investment or loan must be paid back

volatility.ex: Investors are worried about the volatility of the market.
volatility.def: the tendency to change suddenly and unpredictably

risky.ex: Investing all your savings in one company is risky.
risky.def: involving the possibility of loss or danger

regulator.ex: The banking regulator fined the company for breaking the rules.
regulator.def: an official organisation that controls an industry

borrower.ex: Borrowers must repay the loan within five years.
borrower.def: a person or organisation that borrows money

insurer.ex: The insurer paid for the damage to the car.

profitability.ex: The new pricing strategy improved the company's profitability within a single year.
profitability.def: the ability of a business to make a profit

conversion.ex: The conversion of the old warehouse into offices took a year.
conversion.def: the process of changing something from one form or use to another

scandal.ex: The accounting scandal forced the finance director to resign last month.
scandal.def: an event that shocks people because it involves dishonest or wrong behaviour

publicly.ex: The airline publicly apologised for the delays and offered passengers a refund.
publicly.def: in a way that is open to everyone; also owned by the government

governance.ex: Good governance is essential for a successful company.
governance.def: the way a company or country is managed and controlled

rebel.ex: He was a rebel at school but became a successful businessman.
rebel.def: a person who refuses to obey people in authority

restructure.ex: The firm restructured its sales department to focus on online customers.
restructure.def: to organise a company or system in a new way

allowance.ex: Staff receive a travel allowance of fifty dollars a month.
allowance.def: an amount of money given regularly for a particular purpose

warrant.ex: The decision does not warrant such a strong reaction.
warrant.def: an official document giving the right to do something; also a right to buy shares

technological.ex: Rapid technological change is creating new jobs while making others disappear.

shrink.ex: The market for printed newspapers continues to shrink.

foreigner.ex: Many foreigners work for international companies in the city.

pledge.ex: The company pledged to cut its emissions by half.

modest.ex: The company reported a modest increase in profits.
modest.def: not very large in size or amount; also not talking much about your own success

presidency.ex: During her presidency, the association doubled its membership.
presidency.def: the position or period of being president

insider.ex: An insider revealed details of the deal to the press.
insider.def: a person who is part of a group or company and knows secret information

constitutional.ex: The court ruled on a constitutional question about the powers of local councils.
constitutional.def: relating to the basic laws of a country

privatization.ex: The privatization of the national railway was controversial with many passengers.
privatization.def: the sale of a state-owned company to private owners

accordance.ex: Payments are made in accordance with the contract.
accordance.def: agreement with a rule or wish (in accordance with)

activist.ex: Environmental activists protested outside the factory about the pollution in the river.
activist.def: a person who works to bring about political or social change

consultancy.ex: She works for an engineering consultancy that advises on major transport projects.
consultancy.def: a company that gives expert advice to other businesses

lessee.ex: The lessee is responsible for repairs to the property.
lessee.def: a person or company that rents a property under a lease

bust.ex: Many small firms went bust during the crisis.
bust.def: to go bankrupt (go bust); also to break something

rally.ex: Share prices rallied strongly after the company announced better-than-expected results.
rally.def: an increase in prices after a fall

exempt.ex: Small businesses with low turnover are exempt from this new tax.
exempt.def: not required to do or pay something

weaken.ex: The national currency weakened against the dollar after the interest rate cut.
weaken.def: to become or make something less strong

suppress.ex: The company tried to suppress the bad news.
suppress.def: to stop something from developing or being known

prevail.ex: Common sense prevailed, and the meeting ended early.
prevail.def: to be stronger and win; to be common

municipal.ex: The municipal library offers free English classes for adults on Sunday mornings.
municipal.def: relating to a town or city government

hostile.ex: The company's board rejected a hostile takeover bid from a larger competitor.
hostile.def: unfriendly and aggressive; in business, a takeover that is not wanted

gamble.ex: Opening a new restaurant in a quiet area is always a gamble for investors.
gamble.def: a risky action that may succeed or fail

tighten.ex: The bank tightened its lending rules after several customers failed to repay loans.
tighten.def: to make something stricter or firmer

squeeze.ex: Rising energy and transport costs are squeezing the profits of small businesses.
squeeze.def: to put pressure on something so that there is less of it

scrap.ex: The factory sells its metal scrap to a recycling company every month.
scrap.def: old metal or other material that can be used again; also a small piece

petrol.ex: Petrol prices rose again this week, so more people are using public transport.

uncertain.ex: The future of the project is uncertain until the government confirms the funding.

seize.ex: Customs officers seized the illegal goods at the port.
seize.def: to take control of something quickly or by force

beneficiary.ex: She is the main beneficiary of the insurance policy.
beneficiary.def: a person who receives money or another benefit from something

capitalization.ex: The company has a market capitalization of two billion dollars.
capitalization.def: the total value of a company's shares

diplomat.ex: The diplomat spoke three foreign languages and had worked in five different countries.
diplomat.def: a person who represents their country abroad

intent.ex: Both companies signed a letter of intent to work together on the new project.

lessor.ex: The lessor owns the building and rents it to the company.
lessor.def: a person or company that rents property to someone else

obstacle.ex: Lack of funding is the main obstacle to growth.

amortization.ex: The table shows the amortization of the loan over twenty years.
amortization.def: the gradual repayment of a debt or reduction in value of an asset

unfair.ex: Customers complained that the new fees were unfair.
unfair.def: not treating people equally or reasonably

demographic.ex: Demographic changes, such as an ageing population, affect the demand for housing.
demographic.def: relating to the structure of a population, such as age and income

senator.ex: The senator gave a speech about trade policy at the annual business conference.

adoption.ex: The adoption of new accounting software has improved efficiency in the finance team.
adoption.def: the decision to start using something new

privately.ex: The company is privately owned, so it does not have to publish its accounts.
privately.def: without other people being present; also owned by individuals, not the state

plunge.ex: Sales plunged by thirty percent in the first quarter.
plunge.def: to fall suddenly and by a large amount

legally.ex: The contract becomes legally binding once both parties have signed it.

revive.ex: The new manager revived the struggling business by focusing on online sales.
revive.def: to bring something back into use or to a healthy state

intermediary.ex: The bank acts as an intermediary between buyers and sellers.
intermediary.def: acting between two people or groups to help them agree

boast.ex: The hotel's boast is that it has the best view in town.
boast.def: something that a person or place is proud to have
boast.vi: niềm tự hào, điều đáng khoe

discourage.ex: High fees discourage customers from using the service.
discourage.def: to make someone less likely to do something

fate.ex: The fate of the factory will be decided next week.
fate.def: what happens to someone or something in the end

widen.ex: The company plans to widen its range of products.
widen.def: to become or make something wider or broader

devise.ex: We need to devise a new marketing strategy.
devise.def: to plan or invent a new way of doing something

speculation.ex: There is speculation that the firm will be sold.
speculation.def: buying things in the hope of a quick profit; also guessing without full information

fighter.ex: She is a fighter and never gives up.
fighter.def: a person who keeps trying and does not give up
fighter.vi: người kiên cường, không bỏ cuộc

grip.ex: The new manager quickly got a firm grip on the company's finances.
grip.def: to hold something tightly; to have a strong effect on

compel.ex: The new law compels companies to publish their salaries.
compel.def: to force someone to do something

slowdown.ex: There is a slowdown in the housing market.
slowdown.def: a reduction in speed or activity, especially in the economy

suspicion.ex: The sudden increase in profits raised suspicion among the auditors.
suspicion.def: a feeling that something is wrong or that someone is guilty

dump.ex: The council fined a company for leaving old electronics at an illegal dump.
dump.def: a place where rubbish is left

bail.ex: The government had to bail out the bank to protect customers' savings.
bail.def: money paid to free an accused person until trial; also rescuing a failing company

surrender.ex: You must surrender your old passport when you get a new one.
surrender.def: to give up something or stop fighting

certainty.ex: There is no certainty that prices will fall.

rebuild.ex: It took the company two years to rebuild its reputation.

corrupt.ex: The corrupt official was removed from his job.
corrupt.def: acting dishonestly for money or personal gain

bold.ex: The company made a bold decision to enter the Asian market.

handful.ex: Only a handful of customers complained about the new opening hours.

respective.ex: The two managers returned to their respective offices.
respective.def: belonging separately to each of the people or things mentioned

odds.ex: The odds of winning the contract are good.
odds.def: the probability that something will happen

allegation.ex: The company strongly denied the allegations of fraud made in the newspaper report.
allegation.def: a statement that someone has done something wrong, without proof

downward.ex: The chart shows a downward trend in sales.

depreciate.ex: New cars depreciate quickly in their first year.

digit.ex: Your new security PIN must contain four digits and should not be easy to guess.
digit.def: any of the numbers from 0 to 9

provoke.ex: The sudden price increase provoked many complaints from regular customers.
provoke.def: to cause a reaction, especially an angry one

secular.ex: The country has a secular education system that does not teach any religion.

distress.ex: The company was in financial distress after losing its main client.
distress.def: a state of serious financial difficulty; also great worry or sadness
distress.vi: tình trạng khó khăn (tài chính); sự đau khổ

accountability.ex: Managers must take accountability for the decisions their teams make.
accountability.def: the fact of being responsible for your decisions and actions

incorporation.ex: The certificate of incorporation shows when the company was founded.
incorporation.def: the legal process of forming a company

diplomatic.ex: She gave a diplomatic answer to the difficult question.
diplomatic.def: relating to diplomacy; also tactful in dealing with people

formerly.ex: The luxury hotel in the city centre was formerly the headquarters of a bank.

optimization.ex: Search engine optimization helps more people find your website.
optimization.def: the process of making something as effective as possible

shed.ex: The company plans to shed five hundred jobs.
shed.def: to get rid of something, such as jobs or costs

wholly.ex: The firm is wholly owned by the government.

predictable.ex: Sales of ice cream are quite predictable because they rise every summer.
predictable.def: able to be known or expected in advance

chaos.ex: The computer failure caused chaos at the airport.
chaos.def: a state of complete confusion and disorder

impairment.ex: The company recorded an impairment of its assets.
impairment.def: a reduction in value; also damage to a body function

accrual.ex: The accrual of interest begins on the first day of the loan.
accrual.def: an amount of money that builds up over time but has not yet been paid

confront.ex: The new manager decided to confront the problem of low staff morale directly.
confront.def: to deal with a difficult situation directly

exile.ex: The writer lived in exile for many years.
exile.def: the state of being forced to live outside your own country

payback.ex: The payback period for the solar panels is about six years.
payback.def: the time it takes for an investment to return its cost

conviction.ex: She spoke with great conviction about the project.
conviction.def: a strong belief; also a court decision that someone is guilty

continuously.ex: The machines in the factory run continuously, day and night, all week.

reliance.ex: The company's reliance on one customer is risky.
reliance.def: the state of depending on someone or something

clash.ex: There was a clash between the two departments over the budget.

deter.ex: High ticket prices deter many young people from going to concerts.
deter.def: to make someone decide not to do something

condemn.ex: The union condemned the decision to close the factory.
condemn.def: to say strongly that something is wrong

operative.ex: The new safety rules become operative at all of our sites next month.

privatize.ex: The government plans to privatize the postal service.
privatize.def: to sell a state-owned company to private owners

endure.ex: The company endured a difficult year but returned to profit in the spring.
endure.def: to suffer something difficult for a long time

deflation.ex: Economists warn that deflation can be as harmful to growth as high inflation.
deflation.def: a general fall in prices in an economy

fierce.ex: There is fierce competition between the two airlines.
fierce.def: very strong and determined; very intense

instant.ex: The new smartphone app was an instant success with younger customers.

sentiment.ex: Consumer sentiment improved in the second quarter as unemployment fell.
sentiment.def: a general feeling or opinion, especially in a market

centralize.ex: The company centralized all its purchasing in one office.
centralize.def: to bring control under one central authority

sovereign.ex: The country issued sovereign bonds to raise money.
sovereign.def: having full power and independence; relating to a country

strive.ex: We strive to give the best service to every customer.
strive.def: to try very hard to achieve something

bribe.ex: The government official refused to accept a bribe and reported the company to the police.
bribe.def: money or a gift given dishonestly to persuade someone

controller.ex: The financial controller checks every payment before it leaves the company.
controller.def: a person who manages the finances of an organisation

supervision.ex: New staff work under supervision for the first month.
supervision.def: the act of watching over people or work to make sure it is done correctly

endowment.ex: The university's large endowment funds hundreds of scholarships for international students.
endowment.def: money given to an organisation to provide a regular income

reconcile.ex: At the end of each month, the accountant reconciles the bank statements with the company records.
reconcile.def: to make two things agree; to find a way to be friends again

liberty.ex: Customers are at liberty to cancel within fourteen days.
liberty.def: the freedom to live and act as you choose

decent.ex: She earns a decent salary and receives good benefits from her employer.
decent.def: of an acceptable standard; honest and good

appetite.ex: Investors have a strong appetite for green energy.
appetite.def: a desire or demand for something

tobacco.ex: The tobacco industry faces strict rules on advertising.
tobacco.def: a plant whose leaves are dried and smoked in cigarettes

quantify.ex: It is difficult to quantify the benefits of training.
quantify.def: to measure or express something as an amount

corn.ex: The farm grows corn and soybeans, which are sold to food manufacturers.
corn.def: a tall plant grown for its yellow grain; maize

skeptical.ex: Many investors are skeptical about the plan to expand into so many new markets.
skeptical.def: doubtful that something is true or useful

legislative.ex: The legislative changes will affect how all businesses store customer data.

negligence.ex: The company was found guilty of negligence after a worker was injured at the site.
negligence.def: failure to take proper care, causing harm

determinant.ex: Price is the main determinant of demand for many everyday products.
determinant.def: a factor that decides how something happens

icon.ex: Click the printer icon at the top of the page to print your boarding pass.

steep.ex: There was a steep rise in prices last month.

optimism.ex: There is growing optimism among business owners about the economy next year.

faction.ex: Two factions within the board disagreed about the plan.

rig.ex: Workers on the oil rig work twelve-hour shifts.

stall.ex: She runs a fruit stall at the market.
stall.def: a table or small shop in a market

optimize.ex: We need to optimize our delivery routes to reduce fuel costs and delays.
optimize.def: to make something as good or effective as possible

discretionary.ex: Discretionary spending falls when people are worried about money.

mutually.ex: We hope to find a mutually beneficial solution.

refusal.ex: Her refusal to sign the contract surprised everyone.

geographic.ex: The company has a wide geographic reach, with offices on four continents.

policeman.ex: A policeman directed the traffic while the traffic lights were being repaired.

amortize.ex: The cost of the machine is amortized over five years.

loser.ex: There are winners and losers in every market.

consistency.ex: Customers value consistency in quality, so every branch follows the same recipes.

declaration.ex: Travellers must complete a customs declaration form before they leave the airport.

harsh.ex: The company received harsh criticism for the delay.

covariance.ex: The analyst calculated the covariance of the two stocks.

jointly.ex: The project is jointly funded by two universities.

spur.ex: Lower taxes for small firms could act as a spur to investment and job creation.
spur.def: something that encourages an activity or development

socialist.ex: The country had a socialist economy for decades.

browser.ex: Open the payment link in your web browser and enter your booking number.

exaggerate.ex: Don't exaggerate the risks in your report, or the board may reject the project.

triumph.ex: The new product was a triumph for the design team.

tranche.ex: The loan will be paid in three tranches.

baseline.def: a starting point used for comparison
baseline.ex: Last year's sales figures will be used as a baseline.

template.def: a document or pattern used as a model for making others
template.ex: Please use this template when you write your monthly report for the board.

obituary.def: an article about the life of someone who has recently died
obituary.ex: The newspaper published an obituary of the famous architect.

peso.def: the currency of several Latin American countries and the Philippines
peso.ex: The price of the tour was given in Mexican pesos rather than US dollars.

stochastic.ex: The model uses stochastic methods to predict demand.

tribal.ex: Tribal leaders were invited to the meeting about the new mining project.

empower.def: to give someone the power or confidence to do something
empower.ex: The training aims to empower staff to make decisions.

oversight.def: the job of supervising something; also a mistake caused by not noticing
oversight.ex: The project needs better oversight from senior managers.

withhold.def: to refuse to give something; to keep back part of a payment
withhold.ex: The client withheld the final payment until the work was finished.

reprint.def: a new printing of a book or document without major changes
reprint.ex: The publisher ordered a reprint after the first copies sold out.

turmoil.def: a state of great confusion or uncertainty
turmoil.ex: The markets were in turmoil after the announcement.

downside.def: the negative part of a situation
downside.ex: The main downside of the job is the long commute.

conjunction.def: a combination of things happening together (in conjunction with)
conjunction.ex: The event is organised in conjunction with the city council.

hurdle.def: a problem that must be solved before progress can be made
hurdle.ex: Funding is the biggest hurdle for small start-ups.

premier.ex: The hotel is the city's premier venue for conferences.

inability.def: the lack of power or skill to do something
inability.ex: His inability to manage time caused many delays.

autonomous.def: able to make decisions and act independently
autonomous.ex: The company is divided into autonomous business units.

oust.def: to force someone out of a job or position
oust.ex: The shareholders voted to oust the chief executive.

entrepreneurial.def: showing the qualities needed to start and run a business
entrepreneurial.ex: She has a strong entrepreneurial spirit and started her first business at twenty.

hypothetical.def: based on an imagined situation rather than fact
hypothetical.ex: Let's consider a hypothetical example to explain how the tax would work.

boycott.def: to refuse to buy, use or take part in something as a protest
boycott.ex: Thousands of customers boycotted the brand after the scandal became public.

disastrous.ex: The product launch was disastrous because the website crashed on the first day.

undervalue.def: to think that something is worth less than it really is
undervalue.ex: Many investors believe the company's shares are undervalued.

undoubtedly.ex: Undoubtedly, the internet has changed the way we shop.

ratify.def: to make an agreement officially valid by signing or voting for it
ratify.ex: All member countries must ratify the trade agreement before it can take effect.

proclaim.def: to announce something publicly and officially
proclaim.ex: The company proudly proclaimed record profits at its annual meeting.

enrich.def: to improve the quality of something; also to make someone richer
enrich.ex: Reading widely in English can enrich your vocabulary and improve your writing.

clout.ex: Large retailers have a lot of clout with suppliers.

ineffective.ex: The old marketing strategy was ineffective, so sales continued to fall.

syndicate.def: a group of people or companies working together for a business purpose
syndicate.ex: A syndicate of international banks provided the loan for the new airport.

supervisory.def: relating to supervising people or work
supervisory.ex: She has a supervisory role in the department.

dissent.def: to express disagreement with an official view
dissent.ex: Two board members dissented from the decision to close the factory.

synergy.def: the extra benefit from two groups working together
synergy.ex: The merger created synergy between the two companies.

fraudulent.def: dishonest and illegal, intended to cheat
fraudulent.ex: The bank detected several fraudulent transactions on the customer's credit card.

constituent.ex: Sugar is a constituent of many processed foods.

rebound.ex: Analysts expect a rebound in sales next year.

ounce.def: a unit of weight equal to about 28 grams
ounce.ex: Gold is traded on international markets at a price per ounce.

contributor.def: a person or thing that helps to cause something or gives money or work
contributor.ex: Traffic is a major contributor to air pollution.

duly.def: in the correct or expected way
duly.ex: The documents were duly signed by both parties.

imminent.ex: Staff believe that an announcement about the merger is imminent.

empowerment.def: the process of giving people more control over their lives or work
empowerment.ex: The programme focuses on the empowerment of women in business.

void.ex: The contract was declared void because one of the signatures was missing.

alas.def: used to express sadness or regret (old-fashioned)
alas.ex: We hoped to win the contract, but alas, the client chose another supplier.

prod.def: to encourage someone to do something
prod.ex: The new rules prodded companies to cut emissions.

resale.def: the sale of something that has been bought before
resale.ex: The resale value of the car is high.

legitimacy.def: the quality of being legal or acceptable
legitimacy.ex: The legitimacy of the vote was questioned after reports of missing ballots.

inconsistent.def: not staying the same; not in agreement
inconsistent.ex: The results of the new study were inconsistent with earlier research findings.

timber.def: wood used for building or making things
timber.ex: The new office building is made from local timber to reduce its carbon footprint.

intercept.def: to stop someone or something before it reaches its destination
intercept.ex: Customs officers intercepted the shipment at the port.

dismal.ex: Sales were dismal in the first quarter because of the cold weather.

demise.def: the end or failure of something
demise.ex: The demise of the local factory hit the town hard.

intensify.def: to become or make something stronger or more extreme
intensify.ex: Competition between the two budget airlines has intensified this year.

aviation.def: the design, building and flying of aircraft
aviation.ex: The aviation industry recovered quickly after the crisis.
